title: [Chore] Add  `socat` Dependency Installation to `README.md`
body:
This PR proposes updatin `README.md` to explicitly include instructions for adding `socat` as a dependency when setting up `root-vconsole` for `pb-src` development.

Though a small chore, this change should help to communicate requirements in advance of the setup workflow. Instead of the current developer experience, which interrupts the person running `./root-vconsole` for the first time if `socat` isn't installed, this forewarns them of the install, reducing friction during setup.
author: jthodge

comments.body: Good idea, @jthodge!  I'll merge this change now, but the next release will allow (and prefer) ssh into the instance, so this should quickly become moot.  We'll update the instructions then.

title: run-playbit.sh: failed to initialize KVM
body:
OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS

Steps
sudo apt-get install qemu
sudo apt-get install qemu-utils qemu-system

Startup error upon running `./run-playbit.sh`:
Formatting 'disk0.qcow2', fmt=qcow2 size=68719476736 cluster_size=65536 lazy_refcounts=off refcount_bits=16
Could not access KVM kernel module: No such file or directory
2024-11-14T06:43:48.772837Z qemu-system-x86_64: failed to initialize KVM: No such file or directory

I checked and 
> qemu-system-x86 is already the newest version (1:4.2-3ubuntu6.30)
author: anjakefala

comments.body:
Hey @anjakefala, Playbit currently requires KVM.  Here's a diagnostic checklist:

1. Does your CPU support virtualization?

    `grep -E "vmx|svm" /proc/cpuinfo`

If this returns output, your CPU supports virtualization.  If not, you may need to enable KVM in your BIOS settings. Otherwise, KVM won't work on your system and neither will this version of Playbit.

2. Are the KVM kernel modules loaded?

    `lsmod | grep kvm`

If you don't see kvm_intel (for Intel CPUs) or kvm_amd (for AMD CPUs), you need to load the modules:
```
sudo modprobe kvm
sudo modprobe kvm_intel  # for Intel CPU
# OR
sudo modprobe kvm_amd    # for AMD CPU
```
3. Does the KVM device exist?

    `ls -l /dev/kvm`

4.  Are you in the correct group?

     `sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER`

You'll need to log out and back in for this change to take effect.

5. Have you installed these packages?

     `sudo apt install qemu-kvm libvirt-daemon-system libvirt-clients bridge-utils`
I set up virtualisation in my BIOS, and now everything works! Thank you!
